text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Spike in 5xx rate from model-serving-runtime (us-west-2). Error rate jumped to ~9% over last 3m; p95 latency up. Auto-escalation -> paging #oncall-alice.k
alice.k: I'm on it. Can someone grab initial impact breakdown? which customers hit, which routes?
ben.sre: Looking at gateway logs — lots of `SIGSEGV` / `OOM` in model-runner processes. Top trace shows `kv_cache_pop()` then `segfault` on GPU workers. Examples attached from host gpu-12.
carla.runtime: Confirmed. Model runner dmesg shows repeated `Out of memory` before segfaults. Likely paging / kernel OOM from large-batch requests. Repro on staging with long context sequences.
david.support: Support is seeing elevated 502/504s for customer acct-846 and streaming sessions from product-trial users. CS informing customers: investigating, possible degraded responses.
alice.k: Triage plan: 1) throttle large-batch and long-seq requests at gateway (reduce max_tokens + disable burst batching). 2) isolate failing hosts, restart model-runner on those hosts. 3) route traffic to fallback smaller model variant. 4) engage infra if kernel-level OOMs continue.
ben.sre: Quick mitigation applied: lowered max_batch_size from 64 -> 16 for model family "rw-large-v1" via feature-flag. Also disabled prefix concatenation cache for that pool. Rolling config to all us-west-2 nodes (ETA ~60s).
carla.runtime: I'm rolling restarts for gpu-12 and gpu-15 now with `systemctl restart model-runner` and block device checks. Patching runner to log pre-alloc sizes. If restarts fail, we'll cordon host and evict pods.
infra-bot: evict-job: scheduled eviction of non-critical jobs on gpu-12,gpu-15 -> started.
ben.sre: After throttles, 5xx decreased to ~2.1% in 4 minutes. p95 latency improving. Still seeing occasional segfaults on gpu-15.
alice.k: Good. Customer impact: acct-846 and trial cohort hit 30-40% error rates at peak. No critical SLA-tier customers impacted so far. Notifying support to update status page with degraded performance.
david.support: Status page draft: "We are investigating increased error rates for text-generation in US-WEST-2. Some requests may see 5xx errors or timeouts. Mitigations are in progress." Will post in 5.
carla.runtime: On gpu-15 I see `oom-killer` events: kernel reclaim failed. Kernel logs show `oom_reaper` invoked. Looks like memory limit on GPU driver + host DPDK pinned pages. I'm going to try disabling continuous batching on that runner binary and restart.
ben.sre: If kernel OOM persists after config changes, suggest scaling out runners in another AZ and failing over to them. I've started provisioning 4 extra instances in us-west-2b.
alice.k: Agreed. Also enable automatic fallback policy: route heavy requests to `rw-medium-v1` until we confirm stability. Carla, coordinate a canary migration (5% -> 20% -> 100%).
carla.runtime: Canary started: 5% of traffic diverted to medium variant. Monitoring logs for regressions. Also adding extra per-request memory checks to runner (temporary guard rails).
elaine.prod: Heads up — product telem shows a few customer-facing flows reliant on streaming completion. If fallback reduces quality, we should prepare messaging to key accounts.
david.support: Noted. I'll flag acct-846 as P2 with product for followup once we stabilize.
ben.sre: Patch attempt: added extra guard in model-runner to cap kv_cache allocations per-request and disabled prefetch for long-context. Deployed to canary. Logs show no new segfaults in canary hosts after 8 minutes.
alice.k: Nice work. Timeline: 00:00 initial alert -> 00:05 throttle -> 00:10 restarts + evictions -> 00:20 fallback canary -> 00:30 rollback throttles as stability improves. We need a short postmortem but first get stable.
carla.runtime: Still seeing a single host with recurrent kernel OOM (gpu-22). I'm going to cordon+drain it and run `dmesg` capture for devtools. If hardware is flaky, swap instance.
infra-bot: instance-swap: initiated replacement for gpu-22.
ben.sre: Error rate now ~0.5% and trending down. p95 latency near normal. No further segfaults on active hosts.
david.support: Status page updated and sent to customers: "Mitigations applied; performance recovering. We will provide an update after full root cause analysis." Reactions positive.
alice.k: Moving to next phase: create incident ticket, assign owners for RCA (carla runtime lead, ben infra), timeline capture, and impact quantification. Also list immediate action items for hotfix (kv cache safe checks, smarter batching thresholds).
carla.runtime: Acknowledged. I'll collect runner logs, kernel oops, and reproduce minimal repro on staging. Will propose code change to gracefully fail large requests instead of causing OOM.
ben.sre: I'll correlate host-level metrics, GPU memory consumption traces, and placement decisions to see if scheduled batch packing caused hotspots.
elaine.prod: I'll coordinate comms with affected accounts and make sure we have product-side guardrails for customers using long-seq features.
alice.k: Thanks all. If anything spikes again, re-open paging. Otherwise we'll keep monitoring for 2h and kick off RCA doc.
incident-bot: Incident marked as "stabilized" by on-call (alice.k). Start collecting logs and create incident-ticket-2701239876.
carla.runtime: Uploading logs and the `dmesg` capture to the incident ticket now. I'll draft mitigation PR with tests to limit request memory usage.
ben.sre: Leaving a checklist in the ticket: reproduce, patch, canary, ramp, retire old config. Estimate 4-6h to patch and verify.
alice.k: OK closing thread for active paging. Follow-ups in incident-ticket-2701239876 and postmortem channel. :thumbsup:
